reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's commitment to helping the Hebrew people through multiple actions: (1) Yahweh directly commands David to 'shepherd My people Israel' (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ...אַתָּה תִרְעֶה אֶת־עַמִּי אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל), which implies care and support; (2) Yahweh actively delivers Israel from enemies ('וַיּוֹשַׁע יְהוָה תְּשׁוּעָה גְדוֹלָה' - Yahweh provided great salvation/deliverance); and (3) Yahweh's presence is explicitly with the leader ('וַיהוָה צְבָא֖וֹת עִמּוֹ'). The text further affirms that David's kingship occurred 'according to the word of Yahweh' (כִּדְבַר יְהוָה), indicating divine purpose. In the biblical shepherd metaphor, shepherding encompasses both protection and provision for the people's welfare.
